chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Hakim said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both)

about a man who married his female slave to another man, telling her, 'When the husband dies, you are free.' The husband died. He said, 'When the husband dies, she is free; she observes the waiting period of the one whose wife died, and she has no inheritance from him because she only became free after the husband's death.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a female slave married by her master with a condition of freedom upon the husband's death?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), the condition of manumission is treated as a contingent event that takes effect upon the husband's death, thereby establishing her status as a widow for the purpose of the waiting period (iddah). However, because her freedom is not acquired until the moment of death, she is excluded from inheritance, illustrating the Shia juristic distinction between the timing of emancipation and the vesting of marital rights. This highlights the precision of conditional manumission (kitabah or tadbir) in classical fiqh.
